memo.verdict: Neutral; park, with two named re-entry triggers; medium conviction. The record parks Halma (HLMA-GB) at 3,464 pence (2026-10-01) because the 'Modal return' is D (about 12.5 percent a year over eighteen months, about 12.1 percent a year over three years, against the 20 percent bar) and the primary 'Target Setup' fit is C, not because the case is poor; the lean is constructive on the business and neutral on the shares at this price. The park rule is not triggered: management B, business quality B, predictability B, trackability C. Progress on either trigger: a price at or below about 3,150 pence, where the modal path clears 20 percent a year at eighteen months; or hard evidence on Avo Photonics (a transaction announced, a second hyperscaler customer, or FY28 photonics guidance at or above 10 percent growth with the merchant ramp visible), which would move the cleared odds to likely and the 'Modal return' to B. First check: first-half FY27 results on 19 November 2026.
case: - The thesis: Halma is an oversold-compounder case, not a change case. A serial acquirer of life-safety, environmental and healthcare niches with 23 consecutive years of record adjusted profit, whose shares at 3,464 pence sit in the bottom decile of their own ten-year multiple range because a fifth of the group, a contract manufacturer with one hyperscaler customer, is losing its claim on that customer's growth. The core four-fifths is upgrading margins and compounding through a record acquisition year, and that is not yet in the price; but on the modal path the return is about 12 percent a year, so the case is compelling only on the branch where the Avo discount clears, at possible odds.

- The change that caused the fall is real and external. Avo's growth is guided to halve from 52 percent (FY26) to 30 percent (FY27); the customer routes incremental optical-circuit-switch volume to merchant suppliers who own their intellectual property. Lumentum guides to its first triple-digit-million OCS revenue quarter, has a multi-year multi-billion-dollar agreement from the second half of 2026, and expects to be the customer's largest supplier in early 2027; Coherent has more than ten active OCS engagements and a 2 billion USD addressable market; Silex disclosed Google as 24 percent of its 2025 sales. Redburn downgraded to Neutral on FY28 share-loss risk (10 and 24 September 2026). The customer's spending is rising, not falling: Alphabet 2026 capital expenditure guidance 195 to 205 billion USD from 180 to 190 billion USD, a significant further increase expected in 2027. The question is Avo's share of a growing pie.

- The change the company made is real and internal. FY27 adjusted EBIT margin guidance raised to 23.5 to 24.0 percent from about 22.7 percent on 24 September 2026 (about 100 basis points, about 4 percent of EBIT; slightly more than half operational execution, the rest margin-accretive deals and disposals); a record 515 GBPm of acquisitions at about 12x EBIT; the first run of disposals in years (83 GBPm); the core growing 6 to 7 percent organically, its ten-year average, so it is not a false friend hidden behind photonics.
counter_case: - At Building Block 1, in its strongest form: Halma's two-year acceleration was a single customer's capital cycle passing through a contract manufacturer, and that customer has now decided to buy its optical switches from merchants who own their intellectual property and their scale. Avo's revenue, about 20 percent of the group and about half of Environmental & Analysis, flattens in FY28 and declines from FY29 as Lumentum takes first the incremental and then the base volume; consensus, which still models 30 to 35 percent photonics growth for FY27 and only a gentle fade, is 5 to 10 percent too high on FY28 and FY29 EPS; the margin upgrade is partly a temporary mix effect that reverses as Avo's volumes and the healthcare rebound normalise; the serial-acquirer arbitrage is narrowing as rates stay at 5 to 6 percent and multiples paid drift to 12 to 16x; so the multiple, far from recovering to 26.7x, continues toward the sector's 16 to 20x as a premium that peaked at 106 percent against a 70 percent average keeps normalising. The evidence for it is the strongest in the record: Lumentum's agreement and guidance; Silex's 24 percent disclosure; Redburn's downgrade and FY28 share-loss call; Microsoft and AWS engineers on internalisation of manufacturing recipes and co-packaged optics capping a contract manufacturer's upside; Avo's average growth of 50 percent a year for three years driven entirely by one client; the 12.1x deal multiple; return on total invested capital drifting from 16.3 percent in 2015 to 14.4 percent in 2024. On the return: Avo's about 500 GBPm of revenue declining 20 percent in FY29 takes about 4 points off group revenue growth and about 5 percent off FY29 EPS to about 151 pence; at 22.5x the three-year return is about 7 percent a year, at 20.2x about 4 percent.

- Concessions: the share-loss risk is real and not in consensus; neither the record nor the sell-side can see inside the relationship; the modal path already assumes Avo flattens, so the counter-case is a matter of degree; the margin step-up has a temporary component; the fair multiple with Avo retained and discounted is about 24.0x, not 26.7x, which is why the record blends. The record makes no claim that the core covers the enterprise value: FY27 core adjusted net income of about 401 GBPm (four-fifths of about 501 GBPm) is worth about 2.9 billion GBP at 7.2x, about 6.4 billion GBP at about 16x and about 10.7 billion GBP at 26.7x against a market capitalisation of about 13.2 billion GBP; the core does not cover the market value below about 33x on that line, so the downside is not bounded by the core.
triggers: - Progress triggers: price at or below about 3,150 pence (modal path clears 20 percent a year at eighteen months; about 2,830 pence at three years); or hard evidence on Avo: a transaction announced, a second hyperscaler customer, or FY28 photonics guidance at or above 10 percent growth with the merchant ramp visible. Either moves cleared odds to likely and the 'Modal return' to B. A price of about 3,440 pence would make the 'Modal return' a C.

- First check: first-half FY27 results on 19 November 2026 (margin against 23.5 to 24.0 percent; photonics tracking 30 percent; healthcare order book); a third-quarter update around March 2027; FY27 results in June 2027 with FY28 guidance; FY28 results in June 2028, the year share loss is expected to show.

- Avo volume: Alarm at Avo growth below 20 percent in FY27, or Lumentum named the customer's largest supplier with Avo volumes flat; Invalidate at Avo organic growth negative in FY28, or the customer's allocation shifted entirely to merchant platforms. Toward the bull: a second hyperscaler customer or a multi-year volume commitment.
- Merchant outsourcing: Alarm at Lumentum stating it holds the majority of the customer's total, not incremental, volume.

- Core engine: Alarm at core organic growth below 5 percent for two halves or margin below 23 percent; Invalidate at margin below the 19 percent floor. Margin guidance cut below 23 percent changes the view.
- The multiple: Alarm below 20.2x, the five-year low; no Invalidate, a multiple is an output.
